drafts.headline: Screaming Clerk Wins Trading Tournament
drafts.body:
Junior clerk Kenji Al-Jamil won the annual Port-Side Margin Call tournament on Friday by shouting down a ventilation shaft.

The tournament began during the third-shift coolant flush.

Al-Jamil, representing the Sector Four Soy Syndicate, faced a steep six-point deficit against the veteran valve-trader Sunita Patel.

Patel had dominated the early rounds with her signature low-frequency drone, which easily bypassed the cabin air-filters.

But Al-Jamil changed his tactics.

In the final minute, as nitrogen futures ticked downward, he discarded his regulatory throat-mic and leaned into the bare shaft.

He screamed a buy-order for twelve thousand tonnes of wet feed.

The sound waves travelled down the steel pipe at three hundred metres per second, bypassing the ship's sluggish copper network.

His left eardrum ruptured instantly.

The acoustic signal reached the third-deck engine-room floor six seconds before the computerised ticker could update.

The board confirmed his victory.

"I heard a wet pop," Al-Jamil said through a translator in the ship's medical bay.

"But we secured the nitrogen."

To honour his effort, the syndicate has awarded him a new copper ear-plug.
drafts.scene: A clerk in a grease-stained tunic leans precariously over a gaping circular ventilation grate, his mouth wide in a yell while holding one hand over his bleeding ear.
